judge_assessment.explanation: I re-derived every polynomial and the judge's account is exact. f(2) = 8-16+2+6 = 0; x^3-4x^2+x+6 = (x-2)(x-3)(x+1); x^3+2x^2-5x-6 = (x+1)(x+3)(x-2); h(1/2) = 0 and 2x^3-x^2-8x+4 = (2x-1)(x-2)(x+2); x^3-4x^2+2x+4 = (x-2)(x^2-2x-2) giving 1 plus/minus sqrt3; 3x^3-x^2-12x+4 = (3x-1)(x-2)(x+2); x^3-x^2-13x-3 = (x+3)(x^2-4x-1) giving 2 plus/minus sqrt5; the quartic factors to (x+1)(x+2)(x-2)(x-3); x^3-x^2+4x-4 = (x-1)(x^2+4) giving 1 and plus/minus 2i; and 4x^3-8x^2-x+2 = (x-2)(2x-1)(2x+1). The judge's second claim is also supported: problem 12's model answer distinguishes an exhausted rational-candidate list from the existence of a non-rational real root, and does so with a concrete sign change - u(-1) = 1 > 0 and u(0) = -1 < 0 - rather than an appeal to authority. Standards are tagged HSA-APR.B.3, the map's 'Polynomial zeros & graphs' row, matching the contract; unlike five other cases in this shard, final_response.md makes no false claim about the map. I agree with the verdict and the reasoning; I record one small slot-coverage gap below that changes neither.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 12 is the right way to close a rational-root ladder and should be the template for synthesis items in this instructional mode. u(x) = x^3 - 3x - 1 has candidate list {1, -1}, both nonzero, and the item asks why that does NOT mean 'no real zeros'. It is correctly typed manual, it prints \noansline instead of a misleading answer line, and the key requires two specific points while naming a second acceptable argument (odd degree forces a real zero) rather than accepting hand-waving.

The skeletons rotate without repeating: evaluate a candidate, finish a started division, factor completely over the integers, a leading coefficient of 2 and then of 3 that put halves and thirds on the candidate list, an irrational leftover (1 plus/minus sqrt3, 2 plus/minus sqrt5), a quartic that needs the routine run twice, and a non-real leftover (plus/minus 2i).
Problems 1 and 2 are deliberately split - test one candidate, then use that result to divide and finish - so the worked pattern is executed by the student in two graded steps rather than read.

The answer key prints the candidate list for every problem, not just the candidate that worked, which is what the worksheet directions demand ('Show your candidate list and your division work - both are part of the answer').

root_causes.description: Problem 10 asks two questions and records one. After 'Find all zeros of s(x) = x^3 - x^2 + 4x - 4, including any non-real zeros' the stem adds 'State how many zeros the theorem itself was able to supply' - a second printed response slot that the answer key answers in full but that no verify entry covers, machine or manual.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 10: 'Find all zeros of s(x) = x^3 - x^2 + 4x - 4, including any non-real zeros. State how many zeros the theorem itself was able to supply.'
verify.json id 10 is a single zeros entry expecting [1, '2*I', '-2*I'].
answer_key.pdf problem 10 answers the second question separately: 'Answer to the second question: the theorem supplied exactly one zero, the rational one.'

improvements.title: One verify entry per printed response slot, including enumerated sub-parts and trailing second questions
improvements.proposed_change: Require the verify JSON to carry as many entries under an id as the printed problem has response slots. Sub-parts written as (a)/(b)/(c), and trailing extra questions ('Then check: what is m<A?', 'State how many zeros the theorem supplied'), each need their own entry - machine-typed where a value is computable, manual where it is not. Add a lint that, per problem segment of the worksheet .tex, counts enumerated \item sub-parts and \ansline / \answerline occurrences and fails when that count exceeds the number of verify entries sharing the id. curr-334 already satisfies this and should be cited in SKILL.md as the pattern to copy.
improvements.regression_test: New fixture from curr-301 problem 4: a stem enumerating (a) write the converse, (b) compute QR, (c) explain why PQRS makes the converse false, paired with the single verify entry {"id": 4, "type": "distance", "expected": 3}. The lint must fail with 'problem 4: 3 printed slots, 1 verify entry'. The current tree passes this fixture - it is what shipped.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the largest verification blind spot in the shard: sheets that read as fully verified while a third of what the student writes is unrecorded, and answer keys whose Quick Answers bank prints one value for a two-answer question.
improvements.risk: Low-medium. The \item count is a heuristic: a sub-part that is pure scaffolding ('redraw the two triangles separately first') is not a response slot and would false-positive. Let the author mark such an item so the exclusion is auditable rather than silent.

case_summary: The cleanest Algebra 2 case in my shard. All eleven machine items and all eight study-guide items verify independently and every factorization is complete; the difficulty ramp is real (single candidate test, then a non-unit leading coefficient, then an irrational leftover, then a quartic run twice, then a non-real leftover, then a conceptual synthesis); problem 12 is correctly manual with \noansline and a two-point grading rubric; and the standards tag HSA-APR.B.3 is the map's own row for polynomial zeros, with no false claim about the map anywhere in the delivered response. The only gap I found is minor: problem 10's second printed question - how many zeros the theorem itself supplied - is answered in the key but has no verify entry of either kind. I agree with the judge's ACCEPT and with the reasoning behind it.
